source: Wikipedia (2026) Minimum description length
finding: NML (Shtarkov) code is minimax-optimal and central to MDL but has no Bayesian equivalent. Bayes marginal-likelihood codes with Jeffreys prior match NML asymptotically for exponential families.
numbers: Claim as stated in the article; marginal codes and NML differ for short sequences.
quote: normalized maximum likelihood code 'has no equivalent in Bayesian inference'
limits: Secondary source; verify with Grunwald and Roos 2019 (see 03_statistical_mdl).
agent_relevance: Selection by code length is not always selection by posterior; pick the code deliberately.

source: Wikipedia (2026) Minimum description length
finding: MDL model selection equals BIC for large n. MDL needs no assumption that the true process is in the model class; MML is fully subjective Bayes.
numbers: BIC identity holds for large samples only.
limits: Secondary source.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on BIC-like penalties for tiny sample sizes (a handful of examples in a prompt).

source: Wikipedia (2026) Minimum description length
finding: Coin example: a flexible biased-coin class has total codelength above 1000 bits for the data, so MDL does not accept the biased-coin hypothesis even though the best member fits better.
numbers: Illustrative example.
limits: Teaching example, not an experiment.
agent_relevance: Fit alone is not evidence; charge the cost of the hypothesis class. Supports G3.

source: Grunwald and Langford (2004) Suboptimal Behavior of Bayes and MDL in Classification under Misspecification
finding: Proved: for a fixed distribution D, Bayes (MAP, full posterior) and two-part MDL classifiers stay inconsistent for all large m. Error stays away from the best achievable in the class.
numbers: Failure probability at least 1 - 3exp(-2 m eps^2)-type bound; applies to heavy-tailed priors meeting their conditions.
quote: Bayes and MDL can be inconsistent in the sense that they asymptotically overfit
limits: Needs countable classifier set turned into misspecified probability models; not a result about all Bayes.
agent_relevance: Priors do not rescue a misspecified hypothesis space; prior-weighted selection can overfit forever. Keep held-out checks (G3).

source: Grunwald and Langford (2004) Suboptimal Behavior of Bayes and MDL in Classification under Misspecification
finding: Size of the failure: the gap 0.5H(mu) - mu peaks at mu = 1/5, giving a 0.1609 error gap. Theorem 3 bounds the discrepancy below H(mu).
numbers: Max gap 0.1609 at best-in-class error mu = 0.2 (theory, not experiment).
limits: Worst-case construction.
agent_relevance: Failure can be about 16 points of error in the worst case: large enough to matter.

source: Grunwald and Langford (2004) Suboptimal Behavior of Bayes and MDL in Classification under Misspecification
finding: A consistent alternative exists: a randomised ORB algorithm is consistent for all priors with non-zero mass (Theorem 1).
numbers: Theorem 1; asymptotic.
limits: Authors warn only some standard variants of MDL and Bayes are covered.
agent_relevance: Use tempered or held-out-calibrated weights over hypotheses instead of raw posterior weight.

source: Vitanyi and Li (2000) Minimum Description Length Induction, Bayesianism, and Kolmogorov Complexity
finding: Ideal MDL equals Bayes with the universal (algorithmic) prior: minimise K(H) plus log-loss of data given H. Valid under the Fundamental Inequality: data random relative to H, and H random relative to the prior.
numbers: Theory; additive constants only.
limits: Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable; constants depend on the reference machine.
agent_relevance: Priors are really a choice of description language; for an LLM agent the model's own token probabilities define the prior.

source: Vitanyi and Li (2000) Minimum Description Length Induction, Bayesianism, and Kolmogorov Complexity
finding: Two-part code is never shorter than the best one-part code. They argue compression is almost always the best strategy for hypothesis identification and prediction. Restricting to finite sets gives Kolmogorov minimal sufficient statistic.
numbers: Theory.
limits: Fails for hypotheses that are not random relative to the prior.
agent_relevance: Prefer one-part (predictive) code lengths over crude two-part counts of program size when scoring candidates.

source: Lotfi et al. (2023) Bayesian Model Selection, the Marginal Likelihood, and Generalization
finding: Marginal likelihood (Bayesian Occam, the code length of a Bayes mixture code) can be negatively correlated with generalisation. With Laplace LML on CNNs and ResNets, Spearman correlation with test accuracy is positive for prior precision 100 and turns increasingly negative as precision falls.
numbers: Spearman rho vs Laplace BMA test accuracy on CIFAR models; precision 1e2, 1e-1, 1e-3. Exact rho values not recovered from text.
limits: Laplace approximation is itself sensitive to prior variance and parameter count.
agent_relevance: Selection by prior-weighted evidence depends strongly on prior scale. Do not trust it with vague priors.

source: Lotfi et al. (2023) Bayesian Model Selection, the Marginal Likelihood, and Generalization
finding: LML correlation with BMA test log-likelihood is positive for small data and negative for larger data on 6 CIFAR-10 architectures (DenseNet121 and GoogLeNet train faster but rank worse with more data than ResNet-18 and VGG19). The conditional marginal likelihood (CLML) stays positive.
numbers: Six architectures; varying CIFAR-10 sizes.
limits: Asymptotic consistency of LML needs the true model in the class; not reached in practice.
agent_relevance: Early terms of a prequential code measure the prior, not predictive skill. Score candidates on later (held-out) code length.

source: Lotfi et al. (2023) Bayesian Model Selection, the Marginal Likelihood, and Generalization
finding: Type-II marginal likelihood optimisation can overfit (a GP learns an overfit mean and is overconfident) and underfit. CLML is a partial remedy and scales to thousands of hyperparameters in deep kernel learning.
numbers: GP regression demo; deep kernel learning.
limits: Partial remedy only.
agent_relevance: Support for scoring on later-prefix performance rather than total evidence.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: Tested the martingale property (necessary for an exchangeable Bayesian learner) on Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B, GPT-3 (2.7B, 170B), GPT-3.5, GPT-4. Bernoulli data with n=50: mostly consistent for short continuations m=n/2, frequent violations at m=2n.
numbers: Means 0.3, 0.5, 0.7; n=50; m in {25,100}; bootstrap CIs against a Beta(1,1) reference Bayes model; GPT-4 deviates already at short m.
limits: Small synthetic tasks; number-token formatting.
agent_relevance: LLM in-context belief is not coherent Bayes; code-side aggregation (G5) is safer than trusting the model's own posterior.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: Gaussian experiment (mean -1, n=100, m=50): all models except GPT-3.5 clearly violate the martingale property. Synthetic natural-language task (n=80, m=40): GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 deviate from the reference posterior.
numbers: Test statistics T1 (g(z)=z, z^2) and T2. GPT-3.5 did better than GPT-4 but worse than GPT-3-170B.
limits: Authors suggest instruction tuning hurts Bayesian coherence; not proven.
agent_relevance: Instruction-tuned agents may be the least Bayes-like; do not assume posterior behaviour.

source: Falck, Wang, Holmes (2024) Is In-Context Learning in LLMs Bayesian? A Martingale Perspective
finding: Epistemic uncertainty vs data size: Llama-2-7B and GPT-3.5 shrink slower than Bayes. GPT-3.5 is overconfident with few samples. GPT-3-170B and Mistral-7B scale closest to Bayes.
numbers: Bernoulli mean 0.5 with fractional posteriors as a weaker reference.
limits: Only order-of-magnitude agreement even for the best models.
agent_relevance: Small-sample overconfidence is a known failure; widen intervals when examples are few.

source: Arora, Jurafsky, Potts, Goodman (2025) Bayesian scaling laws for in-context learning
finding: A Bayesian ICL law (prior over tasks times per-example likelihood terms) fits GPT-2 ICL curves on synthetic GINC. Interpolation NRMSE about 0.027-0.028 for all laws; extrapolation from the first 5 percent of points: Bayesian 0.0493 vs 0.0621, 0.0814, 0.1138 for the other laws.
numbers: Table 1 values as read from text extraction; the text says Bayesian is best at extrapolation. Bayesian law has 3M+1 parameters.
limits: Laws are close on interpolation. On real LLMs most comparisons were not statistically significant (paired t-test, p<0.05); only vs the logistic law did it pass.
agent_relevance: ICL curves can be modelled as prior times likelihood; the prior is a measurable parameter.

source: Arora, Jurafsky, Potts, Goodman (2025) Bayesian scaling laws for in-context learning
finding: SFT and DPO mainly change the prior over tasks, not task knowledge. On Llama 3.1 8B Base vs Instruct, instruction tuning lowered the prior of unsafe behaviours but many-shot jailbreaking still saturated the posterior.
numbers: Real LLMs from 1B to 405B; 50 many-shot prompts per dataset and model.
limits: SFT/DPO study was synthetic and low-data; DPO also suppresses favoured-distribution probabilities and worsens all law fits.
agent_relevance: A strong prior can be overcome by enough evidence; scaffold-side priors matter less once many examples arrive.

source: Xie, Raghunathan, Liang, Ma (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: Proved ICL can emerge as implicit Bayesian inference when pretraining is a mixture of HMMs. On GINC, accuracy rises with number and length of examples; ICL fails for concepts outside the pretraining family.
numbers: 12-layer and 16-layer Transformers share validation loss 1.33 (vocab 50) yet in-context accuracy is 81% vs 85%.
limits: Synthetic HMM data; LSTMs beat Transformers on GINC, unlike real LLMs.
agent_relevance: Same loss, different ICL: a code-length (perplexity) comparison cannot select models for in-context skill.

source: Xie, Raghunathan, Liang, Ma (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: GINC shows sensitivity to example order (wide spread across permutations) and cases where zero-shot beats few-shot.
numbers: Order test follows Zhao et al. 2021.
limits: A Bayes-exchangeable learner would be order-invariant, so order effects show non-ideal behaviour.
agent_relevance: Randomise or average over example order in code; do not trust a single ordering.

source: Zhang, Zhang, Yang, Wang (2023) What and How does In-Context Learning Learn? Bayesian Model Averaging, Parameterization, and Generalization
finding: Attention can parameterise Bayesian model averaging. O(1/T) regret for perfectly pretrained ICL over T prompt examples; pretraining error splits into an approximation part (decays exponentially with depth) and a generalisation part.
numbers: Theory only; no LLM measurements.
limits: Assumes a latent-variable model and perfect pretraining.
agent_relevance: The ideal is averaging over hypotheses, not picking one; weight several candidates.

source: Muller et al. (2022) Transformers Can Do Bayesian Inference
finding: Prior-data fitted networks learn posterior predictives from sampled tasks; they near-perfectly mimic Gaussian processes and give over 200-fold speedups in multiple intractable Bayesian setups vs MCMC or SVI.
numbers: Tasks: GP regression, Bayesian neural nets, small tabular classification, few-shot image classification.
limits: Needs a sampleable prior and in-distribution test tasks.
agent_relevance: Priors can be amortised into a network; the prior decides what is learned.

source: Grau-Moya et al. (2024) Learning Universal Predictors
finding: Meta-trained LSTMs and Transformers on universal-Turing-machine data to approximate Solomonoff induction (the universal Bayes mixture, which equals ideal MDL). UTM data transfers to learning universal prediction strategies.
numbers: Abstract and introduction read; detailed numbers not extracted.
limits: Small networks; approximation of SI only.
agent_relevance: Direct link between MDL-style priors and neural predictors.

source: Lotfi et al. (2024) Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds for Large Language Models
finding: PAC-Bayes compression bounds for GPT-2 small with SubLoRA: document-level Top-1 error bound 96.41%, Top-10 77.90%, Top-100 58.34%, bits-per-dimension bound 12.12 vs random guess 15.62 and original model 70.76.
numbers: GPT-2 small, 124M parameters; LoRA-only BPD bound 13.09; subspace-only 14.59.
limits: Bounds are loose in absolute terms; only compressed pretrained models are bounded.
agent_relevance: Model code length gives a provable generalisation link: MDL used as a bound, not as a Bayes posterior.

source: Lotfi et al. (2024) Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds for Large Language Models
finding: Larger models (GPT-2 variants up to 849M parameters) are more compressible and have better bounds than smaller ones.
numbers: Table 3 and Section 7.1.
limits: Small scale vs frontier LLMs.
agent_relevance: Bigger models are simpler per unit of fit; no case for choosing weaker models on simplicity grounds.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Flight-recommendation task, 5 rounds, 100 test sets per round. Off-the-shelf LLMs (Gemma 2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, GPT-4.1 Mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro) fall far below a Bayesian Assistant and mostly plateau after round 1.
numbers: Bayesian Assistant final-round accuracy about 81 percent (read from figure text extraction); uniform prior, other priors similar.
quote: LLMs fall far short of the standard defined by the Bayesian framework
limits: Simple controlled task; follow-up prompting experiments did not help.
agent_relevance: Do not expect an LLM to update beliefs across rounds; put the update in code.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Fine-tuning on Bayesian Assistant outputs beats fine-tuning on oracle answers. Tuned LLMs agree with the Bayesian Assistant about 80% of the time and generalise to hotel recommendation and web shopping.
numbers: Three 7-9B models; three seeds; error bars are standard errors.
limits: A gap to normative Bayes remains; needs training, not just a scaffold.
agent_relevance: Bayes-like updating is learnable by imitation but costs training; our scaffold does the update in code.

source: Sorensen et al. (2022) An Information-Theoretic Approach to Prompt Engineering Without Ground Truth Labels
finding: Choosing a prompt template by mutual information between input and model output, with no labels, gets on average 90% of the way from the average to the best template.
numbers: Many datasets and model sizes; best WiC template reaches 54% accuracy.
limits: Needs output probabilities; weaker on some tasks.
agent_relevance: Label-free selection by information gain (code-length saving) is cheap and good enough for template choice.
